prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. One coherent text-free manuscript miniature, not a card layout.
Medieval Georgian-Persian illuminated manuscript miniature painting for Shota Rustaveli's "The Knight in the Panther's Skin" (ვეფხისტყაოსანი). 16th–17th-century Georgian royal manuscript miniature, Mamuka Tavakarashvili / King Vakhtang VI illumination tradition blended with classical Persian-Safavid tempera miniature. Egg tempera, lapis lazuli, malachite green, vermilion, warm ochre and burnished antique gold leaf on aged ivory-parchment vellum. Stylized faceted rocky cliffs, ornamental cypress and pomegranate trees, intricately patterned arches and domes, expressive courtly figures in medieval Georgian-Eastern attire. Fine controlled contours, delicately patterned fabrics, luminous matte mineral pigments, slightly flattened layered miniature space with expressive narrative gestures. A painted manuscript scene, not photorealism, cinematic rendering, modern digital fantasy or a collage of circular portraits. Reuse referenced character faces and coloring but adapt costume to the actual chronological story scene; Tariel wears ordinary Indian court or military attire in early backstory, his panther skin belongs to his later exile. Exact horizontal 16:10 composition, preferably native 1600x1000 pixels, a single coherent scene framed for a card vignette. Soft natural painted vignette dissolving to warm aged ivory vellum at edges, modest antique-gold floral flourishes at the perimeter, no rigid border. Key faces and gestures comfortably inside the central safe area, no important content cut off. STRICTLY NO TEXT, NO LETTERS, NO CAPTIONS, NO NUMBERS, NO INSCRIPTIONS, NO CALLIGRAPHY, NO BANNERS, NO SCROLLS, NO SIGNATURES, NO WATERMARKS anywhere. Architectural ornament must be purely floral/geometric with no pseudo-writing. If letters are narratively necessary, use a small closed plain unmarked folded paper or sealed envelope, never visible writing or rolled scrolls. All book covers/pages must be plain and unmarked. Do not show graphic blood or gore; imply violent events through gestures, context and intact clothing.
Episode 20 — Reunion at the Cave, Devis' Armor & March via Mulghazanzar to Kadjeti.
Setting: Wilderness and Cave, the interior threshold of Tariel and Asmat's rocky refuge. This is the emotional cave reunion after Avtandil returns directly from Gulansharo with news of Nestan.
Scene: Avtandil leans forward and places a SMALL CLOSED PLAIN UNMARKED FOLDED LETTER PACKET and a narrow patterned blue veil fragment into Tariel's open hands. Tariel, seated on a patterned low carpet, raises one hand toward his heart in overwhelming relief; Asmat stands close beside them holding a small oil lamp. A discreet deep stone recess with three old gleaming suits of empty armor hints at the Devis' treasure that will equip the coming rescue. Warm lamplight and burnished gold illuminate their faces; the cave mouth at the right reveals faceted blue-lilac mountains, a cypress and soft evening sky. Horizontal, intimate three-figure composition, expressive mutual gazes.
Characters: Avtandil has the youthful clean-shaven olive-skinned face and wavy dark hair of reference 2, silver conical helmet, red cloak and bronze armor. Tariel has the mature curly dark hair, strong features, short beard and warm brown skin of reference 3, wearing his late-exile golden panther-skin cap and mantle. Asmat has the gentle dark eyes, wavy brown hair and plain charcoal hooded robe with fine gold edging of reference 4. Exactly these three people, no Nestan or Pridon physically in the cave. The unmarked folded packet conveys Nestan's presence through news only.
Input roles: image1 is the established scene STYLE reference; images2–4 are face/costume identity only. Do not copy circular medallion frames or the poet from image1.
No visible writing on the letter or anywhere else. Absolutely no banners or scrolls. Exact horizontal 16:10, soft natural ivory-parchment vignette.

visual_qa.notes: Three correct cave figures, closed blank letter and blue veil, three empty armor suits. No text, banners or scrolls; consistent soft parchment manuscript scene.
